title: Singapura founded
description: According to the Malay Annals the Sumatran prince Sang Nila Utama founds a kingdom on the island of Temasek and names it Singapura.

title: Wang Dayuan visits Temasek
description: A Chinese traveller describes two settlements on the island, the earliest eyewitness account of Singapore.

title: Fall of Singapura
description: The city is sacked and its last ruler, Parameswara, flees north and later founds Malacca.

title: Portuguese burn the settlement
description: Portuguese raiders destroy the trading post at the river mouth, and the island is of little importance for the next two centuries.

title: Raffles founds a British trading post
description: Stamford Raffles signs a treaty with Sultan Hussein and the Temenggong allowing the East India Company to set up a port.

title: Singapore ceded to Britain
description: The Sultan and the Temenggong give up the whole island to the East India Company in return for payments.

title: Capital of the Straits Settlements
description: The seat of government of the Straits Settlements is moved from Penang to Singapore, by now the busier port.

title: Crown colony
description: The Straits Settlements are transferred from the government of India to direct rule by the Colonial Office in London.

title: Rubber seedlings arrive
description: Rubber plants raised at Kew from Brazilian seed reach the Botanic Gardens, the start of the Malayan rubber industry.

title: Singapore Mutiny
description: About half of an Indian infantry regiment mutinies and kills dozens of soldiers and civilians before being put down within a week.

title: Naval base opened
description: Britain opens the large naval base on which its defence of the Far East is meant to rest.

title: Fall of Singapore
description: General Percival surrenders about 80,000 British Empire troops to a smaller Japanese army, the largest capitulation in British military history.

title: Sook Ching
description: The Japanese military screens the Chinese population and kills thousands of men it judges hostile.

title: Japanese surrender
description: Japanese forces in Southeast Asia surrender to Lord Mountbatten at the Municipal Building.

title: Separate crown colony
description: The Straits Settlements are dissolved and Singapore becomes a colony on its own, apart from Malaya.

title: People's Action Party founded
description: Lee Kuan Yew and others found the party that has governed Singapore since 1959.

title: Self-government
description: Singapore becomes a self-governing state after the People's Action Party wins the election, with Lee Kuan Yew as prime minister.

title: Housing and Development Board set up
description: A new public housing authority begins the building programme that comes to house about four fifths of the population.

title: Operation Coldstore
description: More than a hundred left-wing politicians and trade unionists are arrested and held without trial.

title: Race riots
description: Fighting between Malays and Chinese during a procession for the Prophet's birthday kills 23 people and deepens the rift with Kuala Lumpur.

title: Independence
description: Singapore is separated from Malaysia and becomes an independent republic.

title: National service introduced
description: Parliament passes a law making military service compulsory for young men.

title: Changi Airport opens
description: The new airport begins operations and becomes one of the busiest in Asia.

title: First MRT line opens
description: The first section of the Mass Rapid Transit railway opens between Yio Chu Kang and Toa Payoh.

title: Lee Kuan Yew steps down
description: After thirty-one years as prime minister Lee Kuan Yew hands over to Goh Chok Tong.

title: SARS outbreak
description: The disease reaches Singapore, where 238 people are infected and 33 die before the outbreak is contained in May.

title: Lee Hsien Loong becomes prime minister
description: The elder son of Lee Kuan Yew becomes the country's third prime minister.

title: Death of Lee Kuan Yew
description: The founding prime minister dies aged 91, and more than a million people pay their respects during a week of mourning.

title: Trump–Kim summit
description: Singapore hosts the first meeting between a sitting president of the United States and a leader of North Korea.
